title: Public Transit Delay Tracker
dataSources: ADS-B aircraft snapshots (`adsb:aircraft`), personal flight logbook (`flight:log`), commute trips (`commute:trip`), transit arrivals (`transit:arrival`), geofence events (`geofence:event`), travel documents (`travel:document`), fare quotes (`airprice:quote`).
app: Home ADS-B receiver (dump1090 / readsb / tar1090 JSON feed), personal flight logbook exports, commute/transit APIs, and phone geofence webhooks via Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=transit:arrival
| eval delay_min=round((actual_epoch-sched_epoch)/60,0)
| stats avg(delay_min) as avg_delay, max(delay_min) as worst, count as trips by line
| sort - avg_delay
description: Measures how late your bus or train lines run on average so you can plan around the chronically unreliable ones.
value: Knowing which line is habitually late lets you leave earlier for the one that matters and stop trusting the timetable blindly.
implementation: Ingest realtime transit arrivals against schedule; schedule daily and review average and worst-case delay per line.
visualization: Bar chart of average delay by transit line with worst-case markers.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how late your buses and trains usually are, so you know which ones to give extra time.
